title: Pre-kickoff readiness
sub: Confirm this before the kickoff call, not during it

items.t: Confirm license / entitlement scope matches what's being piloted or demoed (which scanners, how many repos/apps)
Confirm firewall / IP allowlist requirements, especially for self-hosted SCM, on-prem tools, or locked-down networks
If repos are self-hosted or not internet-accessible, confirm whether IP-based repo configuration is needed instead of hostname resolution
Identify who owns each access decision on the customer's side (SSO/IAM admin, repo admin, security lead) so the kickoff isn't stalled waiting on the right person
Complete initial admin login
Review global account settings (scanner defaults, AI Assist, domain management)
Decide SSO vs. local auth; configure SAML/OIDC or LDAP
Create groups and map roles (avoid one-off user-level permissions)
Generate API keys / OAuth clients for CI/CD and IDE integrations, scoped to least privilege
Define the Application hierarchy first (business units, product lines) before creating projects
Decide project structure (per-repo vs. other) and naming conventions
Decide on config-as-code if scan config should live in-repo

title: Scanner configuration
sub: Finish this before connecting repositories in the next step — a connection can auto-trigger the baseline scan

items.t: Set scanner parameters per engine before the first real scan (SAST, SCA, IaC, API Security, Secrets, Container)
Select SAST preset
For large/complex codebases, validate expected project size and structure ahead of time (avoid timeouts / misleading first-scan results)

title: Code repository integration & baseline scan
sub: Confirm scanner configuration above is finished first

items.t: Connect SCM (GitHub / GitLab / Bitbucket / Azure DevOps) — managed vs. self-hosted
Decide on auto-onboarding of new repos
Confirm repository coverage matches what leadership expects
Pick the plugin(s) matching the customer's pipeline (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, GitLab, CircleCI, Bamboo, etc.)

title: Policy, break-build gates & notifications
sub: Decide gating before devs see output, not after

items.t: Define policies — which findings block builds, which just report

Leave break-build off by default. If turning it on for a POV, be upfront that developers will start seeing scan output in their pipeline as soon as it's enabled — agree on a non-critical test repo, or make sure the team is briefed before flipping it on broadly
Set up ticketing/notification integration (Jira, Azure Boards, Slack, Teams, email)
Roll out IDE plugins (VS Code, JetBrains, Visual Studio, Eclipse, Cursor, Windsurf) for teams wanting inline results
Scope Developer Assist / AI remediation adoption separately if in scope
Set up dashboards security/eng leadership will actually look at
Confirm report cadence/format expectations (feeds into Executive Health Checks later)
Scope SAST-to-CxOne migration as its own workstream if applicable
